answer: Coordinated Inlet Pricing. Each agent identity must anchor a unique inbound channel at an inlet node, and every message between distinct identities pays a routing toll proportional to the number of new peer pairs it opens. The toll scales with graph expansion, so a sybil cluster pays for each edge it adds, not just each node. Attackers face rising per-identity costs as the juniper threshold curve steepens; honest agents in a stable grove of recurring peers pay near zero, since repeat channels are toll-free.
